title: Vellum Tech — Security posture & deployment options (intro)
summary: Introductory security posture discovery for Vellum Tech evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Covered SOC 2 / ISO needs, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC mapping, audit logs/retention, envelope encryption / KMS options, data residency and retention windows. Customer concerned about key ownership and long-term retention for PII and logs. Agreed next step: send SOC2 + ISO cert pack, share network diagram and sample RBAC mappings, schedule technical deep-dive with infra and security team week of May 3.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2027-04-28 11:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Recording: yes
- Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Vellum), Diego Ruiz (Head of Security), Maya Chen (Compliance), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Olivia Park (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood inference, and with me is Samir — our solutions lead — quick round robin?
[00:12] Aisha: hi all, aisha here, we'll be evaluating options for hosting our inference stack for a new customer-facing feature, mainly concerned about security and compliance, we'll hand it over to diego and maya after the high level.
[00:25] Diego: yea, want to make sure keys, logs, and retention are solid before we commit.
[00:30] Samir: great, thanks. quick agenda: SOC2/ISO attestation, auth (SSO/SAML/OIDC), RBAC provisioning, audit logs & retention, encryption/KMS, and deployment choices (hosted, dedicated, private). We'll also note the decision criteria you mentioned — latency, cost, and control.
[00:48] Olivia: sounds good.
[00:51] Jordan: do you have an initial preference? Aisha?
[00:55] Aisha: from product pov we'd like hosted for speed, but security expressed interest in private or dedicated if that solves key ownership and auditability issues.
[01:08] Diego: yes, we can't hand over keys to a vendor for some workloads. we need customer-managed keys for PII processing and audit logs retained for at least three years per our contract.
[01:22] Samir: understood. Redwood supports a couple of options — hosted with Redwood-managed KMS, hosted with BYOK via cloud KMS integrations, Dedicated pools with customer KMS bindings, and Private deployments where you retain full key ownership and control of the control plane. apologies if terms get fuzzy — i might say redwood private or private cp.
[01:44] Maya: what's BYOK exactly here — bring your own key? and does that mean you never see the plaintext?
[01:51] Samir: BYOK = you manage master keys in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK / Azure KeyVault). Redwood can be configured to encrypt model artifacts and logs with your CMEKs so we don't hold the root key. For hosted there are two modes: envelope encryption with your KMS for critical data, or fully private deployment where you keep keys and the control plane inside your VPC. In hosted-with-BYOK we still handle the runtime but never have access to the root key — we only get wrapped keys.
[02:18] Diego: okay, we need an architecture diagram to show separation of duties — so legal is happy.
[02:25] Jordan: we'll attach a network diagram and a one-pager on key handling.
[02:30] Liam: on audit logs — can we export raw audit events to our SIEM? we want immutable logs for model queries and admin actions.
[02:39] Samir: yes, Redwood supports streaming audit events to customer-owned S3 / GCS buckets or to SIEM via syslog/forwarder. We keep internal logs for platform ops but those can be disabled or gated; we can set retention policies and an immutable lifecycle with S3 Object Lock if you need WORM.
[03:00] Maya: what about redaction? some model outputs could contain PII and we don't want those kept in plaintext anywhere.
[03:10] Samir: good question — we recommend request-side redaction pipelines before logs hit storage, and we also offer KV prefix caching that can be configured to avoid storing user prompt content. For sensitive workloads the private deployment + customer KMS + on-prem log sinks is the standard.
[03:30] Diego: SOC2 and ISO — do you have recent audits?
[03:36] Jordan: yes, Redwood has a SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001. i'll share the certs and the scope doc; note that some features are out of scope for hosted vs private, so we'll annotate that.
[03:50] Olivia: do you map controls to our requirements? we have a pre-built matrix we prefer vendors to fill.
[03:56] Jordan: we can fill the matrix, yeah. please send the spreadsheet and we'll complete it.
[04:05] Aisha: SSO — we use Okta today; SAML flows and SCIM for provisioning. how's Redwood integrate?
[04:13] Samir: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC, plus SCIM for user provisioning to map to RBAC roles. For dedicated/private customers you can lock down the admin plane to your IdP and enforce enforced MFA.
[04:27] Diego: RBAC — can we map our existing roles and automate provisioning from groups?
[04:31] Samir: yes, SCIM can sync groups -> roles. we also provide fine-grained resource-level permissions (model, route, environment) and token scoping. there's an admin UI and API. Caveat: some legacy model endpoints have slightly different permission surfaces, but we can show mapping examples.
[04:58] Maya: audit trail for admin actions — is there an immutable record showing who promoted a model, who changed a rollout?
[05:05] Samir: yes, every admin change is logged with actor and IP, and we can export the change history. retention is configurable by policy. by default hosted keeps 90 days; enterprise can extend to multi-year retention via S3 buckets.
[05:25] Diego: on network isolation — if we choose dedicated, will our traffic be in isolated GPU pools? what about peering/VPC endpoints?
[05:33] Samir: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and network isolation at the pool level; private gives you a customer-controlled control plane inside your VPC with direct VPC peering options. for hosted we do TLS + private endpoints and region isolation but not full VPC tenancy.
[05:49] Liam: can you do egress control to prevent data leaving region?
[05:53] Samir: yes, for private deployments we can block egress and set region constraints. for dedicated we can pin to region and set routing to customer-managed NAT.
[06:05] Olivia: any compliance limitations we should be aware of? PCI? healthcare?
[06:10] Jordan: we support SOC2/ISO. for HIPAA we have BAAs available for enterprise agreements; PCI has special controls and is harder with third-party managed models — we'll need a deeper compliance scoping call.
[06:25] Maya: can you confirm which logs are considered "platform ops" vs "customer data"? that's a contractual risk for us.
[06:33] Samir: platform ops logs are operational telemetry (GPU metrics, runtime traces) — we classify them as infrastructure telemetry. Customer data includes prompts, user messages, and returned content. We can keep customer data segregated and stream to your storage. We'll provide the exact KLAs in the attestation pack.
[06:52] Diego: encryption in transit and at rest? any FIPS or HSM-backed keys?
[06:58] Samir: TLS for transit, at-rest encryption with AES-256, and we can integrate with HSM-backed CMKs when customers require FIPS/HSM. For on-prem/private you can tie into your HSM or KMS.
[07:14] Aisha: cycle time — how long to spin a private deployment vs dedicated?
[07:19] Jordan: typical timelines: hosted = immediate/short, dedicated = 2–6 weeks depending on sizing and contract, private = 6–12 weeks for VPC and control-plane install and security hardening.
[07:32] Olivia: costs — curious about delta between hosted and dedicated for our expected 10k qpm.
[07:38] Samir: i didn't catch qpm precisely, but we'll run rough sizing. dedicated reduces per-token cost because of reserved capacity and batching; hosted includes more elasticity but variable cost. we'll send a cost model.
[07:51] Diego: can you guarantee redaction and that raw prompts won't be kept beyond retention?
[07:57] Samir: yes, retention is policy-driven; you can set zero retention for request content in prod. For audit reasons you might keep hashes or metadata. We'll show how to configure that.
[08:10] Maya: legal will ask about subpoenas — do you have law enforcement process documentation?
[08:15] Jordan: yes, we'll include our legal process and how we notify customers. For private deployments customers handle their own legal process.
[08:24] Olivia: next steps?
[08:27] Jordan: quick recap and commitments from Redwood: 1) share SOC2 & ISO certs + scope doc; 2) send architecture diagram and KMS/BYOK detail; 3) sample RBAC mapping and SCIM doc; 4) cost model & sizing for 10k qpm; 5) schedule technical deep dive with diego & liam week of may 3.
[08:45] Aisha: that works.
[08:48] Diego: thanks, also can we get a sample contract clause for data retention?
[08:52] Jordan: yes we can provide standard clause examples.
[08:56] Olivia: ok thanks everyone.
[08:59] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up via email with the pack and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[09:06] END
